body.statement: For the separately defined residual-continuity-only compatible-law class, \(\{\tau^P:P\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}=\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subset\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z}\). Its coordinate interval is \([b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)-u_{0,z}(r),b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)+u_{1,z}(r)]\), the continuous-curve image of the conservative endpoint formula in Wang et al., Theorem 5.1 and equations (8)--(9). For the maintained monotone-Lipschitz class, \(\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). A sufficient observed criterion for strict inclusion is the existence of \(z,r_1<r_2\) such that \(u_{1,z}(r_1)+u_{0,z}(r_2)>2L(r_2-r_1)\), because the two endpoint choices permitted by \(\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) violate the \(2L\)-Lipschitz restriction on \(f_{1,z}-f_{0,z}\).
body.justification: The result gives a valid continuous-function sanity reduction and an observable sufficient certificate that curve coupling strictly improves on pointwise bounds.
body.gap: Wang et al.'s endpoint theorem permits independent adversarial completions at each score value and supplies no observed sufficient criterion certifying that joint residual shape strictly contracts its product region.
body.consumer: The sufficient condition identifies profiles and score pairs for which defending the residual-shape sensitivity model can change a treatment-benefit conclusion.
